added_provisions.reason: Section 39(b), an indispensable provision for M056-Q04, requires an intent to prejudice or defraud “any person”. The Notaries Ordinance interpretation section (s.43) defines only “Council of Legal Education”, “High Court Judge” and “Registrar-General”, so nothing in the corpus establishes that the revenue is such a person. Section 39(f) reaches any wilful act or omission by which the notary commits or attempts to commit a fraud in the execution of his office and carries the same liability without that reading. Added as a supporting provision for M056-Q04 with a verbatim excerpt checked against 1-1907/s39.

question_decisions.note: Held. The load-bearing step, that rule (22) of s.31 limits the area in which the notary attests and not the situation of the land, is carried by the statute itself: rule (29) expressly contemplates an instrument affecting land in a district other than the notary's, and s.4A and s.9 fix the area by reference to the warrant and the notary's office. No Roman-Dutch doctrine or case law is needed. All three indispensable provisions stand (PROV-M056-001 and -003 partially_verified on points that do not touch the conclusion); hop count of 3 matches the indispensable edges; enrichment correctly not applied for a keep question; no case law cited.

Held. Sections 38 and 39 of the Notaries Ordinance and sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act carry a complete duties-and-liabilities answer. One claim (CL-M056-Q04-011) is downgraded to disputed and PROV-M056-901 (s.39(f)) added as an alternative route to the same liability. Hop count of 3 matches the indispensable edges; no case law cited; enrichment correctly not applied.

disagreements.researcher_position: Inserting a rental the notary knows to be false in order to save stamp duty is an insertion “with intent to prejudice or defraud any person” within s.39(b) of the Notaries Ordinance, the person prejudiced being the revenue.
disagreements.verifier_position: The Ordinance does not define “person” and the corpus contains nothing that brings the State or the revenue within the word, so the characterisation is an inference rather than a reading of the text. Section 39(f), which catches any wilful act or omission amounting to fraud in the execution of the notary's office, reaches the same conduct without it and has been added as PROV-M056-901.

disagreements.researcher_position: Section 38 of the Notaries Ordinance, which speaks of “any deed”, applies to a notarially attested lease agreement, so the duty to ascertain and insert the true and full consideration governs the rental figure.
disagreements.verifier_position: The researcher's own corpus_gaps entry concedes that “deed” is undefined and that s.31 mostly says “deed or instrument” where s.38 says “deed”. Section 38 is indispensable to M056-Q04; if it does not reach a lease agreement the whole of that answer falls. This needs a lawyer, not a further corpus search.

unsupported_claims: CL-M056-Q04-011 rests on reading “any person” in s.39(b) as embracing the revenue; marked disputed.
CL-M056-Q04-015 carries the same dependency in its s.39(b) limb, though its s.38(2) and s.21 limbs stand on their own; left verified.

The application paragraph of the M056-Q01 gold answer says the notary's acquaintance with the lessor “in fact assists identification”. That is an uncited allusion to s.31 rule (9); the rule (9) text in force at 2021-10 is not in the corpus body (it was substituted by 31-2022 s.16(6)), and no answer_claim asserts the point, so nothing was added.
temporal_issues: PROV-M056-003: the temporal_note asserts rule (29) was untouched by 6-2024 s.3. It was not. Section 3(9) substituted “in the Form F 1” for “in the Form F” in that rule. The amendment lies outside the quoted excerpt, so the substance relied on was in force at 2021-10.

PROV-M056-001: the subsection label “(1)” is the numbering introduced by 4-2024 s.2; at 2021-10 s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance was unnumbered. The excerpt also stops before the operative “shall be in force or avail in law unless” words. The pre-2022 wording of those words is recoverable from 30-2022 s.2 and supports the claim.

PROV-M056-015 (s.31 rule (6)) and PROV-M056-016 (s.34) re-marked unresolved: the corpus holds only the 2022 replacements and neither amending section reproduces the pre-2022 text, so their October 2021 wording cannot be established. Both were already excluded from every claim.

Everything else checks out. 31-2022 ss.11, 16, 17, 18 and 19 and 6-2024 s.3 were read in full and confirm that rules (11), (13), (20)(f) and (22) of s.31, s.21(1)(b) and (c), s.38(1), the quoted part of s.38(2) and s.39(b) stood in the form quoted at 2021-10.
6-2024 s.4 inserted s.38A only and did not alter s.38, as the researcher assumed.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: s.43 of the Notaries Ordinance defines only “Council of Legal Education”, “High Court Judge” and “Registrar-General”; “deed”, “instrument”, “area” and “person” are all undefined, which is what the two disagreements above turn on.
s.33 (no instrument invalid for non-compliance in a matter of form) and s.32 (rules disapplied for certain deeds) were checked and neither cuts across either answer.

The Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990 s.37 charges provincial stamp duty on instruments relating to a transfer of immovable property in the Province, on documents filed in court there, and on motor vehicle transfers. A lease is none of these, so the researcher was right to leave it out. Section 13 of the 2006 Act likewise leaves the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 operating only as to transfers of immovable property, motor vehicles and court documents. The Colombo situation of the building raises no separate provincial duty on this lease.

s.31 rule (20)(e), which requires the attestation to state whether money was paid in the notary's presence as consideration and the actual amount, is at least as much on point for M056-Q04 as rule (20)(f), but it was substituted by 31-2022 s.16(11)(b) and its 2021 wording is not in the corpus, so it was not added.

lawyer_questions: Does section 38 of the Notaries Ordinance, which speaks of “any deed”, govern a notarially attested lease agreement, and is the agreed rent the “consideration” it requires to be ascertained and set forth? Section 38 is indispensable to M056-Q04 and the whole answer to that question depends on it.
Is understating the rent to save stamp duty an insertion “with intent to prejudice or defraud any person” under section 39(b), or should the answer rest on section 39(f) instead?

Is the reading of section 31 rule (22) as limiting the place of attestation rather than the situation of the land the accepted one in practice, as rule (29) suggests? The whole of M056-Q01 turns on it.
What did section 31 rule (6) and section 34 of the Notaries Ordinance say in October 2021? The corpus holds only the 2022 replacements, so the pre-2022 wording had to be left out of both answers.
